description: Vintage FDNY 1977  This 4 alarm department store fire occurred in the Bushwick / Bedford Stuyvesant section of Brooklyn, NYC, NY.( A  2 alarm fire at Bushwick Ave. and Linden street occurred as a direct result of this fire. The 2 alarm was carried as a different event)  The 4 story block wide building on the corner of Broadway and Linden St. was smoldering for hours before the FDNY was called to the scene. This photo was taken just after the rear wall collasped sending a tornado of fire across the adjacent buildings. The heat was so intense that it ignited buildings up to 2 blocks away on Bushwick Avenue.  Engine 218 (foreground) is a spare apparatus. Notice the numbers are put on with masking tape.  Special thanks to Ret. Batt Chief Rich Rewkowski for his research in properly identifying this fire.  Scanned from the original Kodak Extachrome transparency. title: Emergency! (Here's to the GOOD people!)
tags: blur|blurry|emergency|engine|fire|fire engine|fire truck|friend|friendly|friends|help|peace|red|road|truck|unfound|vehicle|Bellingham|Whatcom|praise and curse of the city|moving|motion|friendship|thank you|appreciation|good|positive|suppport|helpful|constructive|harmony|peaceful|cheers|Yeah!|2005|daveward-smaragd|Washington|WA|US|United States|USA|pss:opd=1130290484
description: There are too many people in the world who are devoted to sewing strife, viciousness, and hurt. Through our actions and our attitudes, we all choose sides in the grand scheme of the world. Do we create tension, or do we encourage harmony? Do hurt people, or do we heal? Do we cut people down, or do we raise them up? Do we make new friends, or do we make new enemies? Do we build bridges, or do we burn them? I lost a dear friend in the last 24 hours; somebody who was once a beautiful, good soul has turned out to be quite the opposite. How hurt I am by this discovery can't be understated. And, inevitably, the bad deny that they are bad, instead claiming that there's no such thing, as though this excuses the harm they've done. Why is it that when people do bad, they so seldom have the honesty, the integrity, the responsibility or the spine to admit that they did bad? In my experience, it's because the people who do bad are usually cowards. Honesty, integrity, responsibility and bravery are qualities you almost never find in people who sew strife, discord and pain. The loss of a friend, and the deep, real hurt it has caused has made me appreciate the truly good people even more. So here's to some of the best hearts, souls, minds and eyes on flickr: Quizz, Solea, Nuclear Sky, seawallrunner, _rebekka, Sume, yotababy, Liltrix, Velvet G, Suzanna, Piper, DrJoanne, The Alieness, the8rgrl, O Caritas, Coffee Break, Sarrah, Barefoot Bex, Greeny, TaG, Fatima, IrregularGirl, Eye Candy, Teotwawki, dotpolka, buhny, anselpixel, achuka, yeimaya... and all those flickr friends I know in "real life" -- you know who you are -- and, of course, Betty. That list is so far from complete--it's barely even a start... There really are some great souls here, and some dear friends. I just want each and all of you to know that I appreciate you all. Thank you for your goodness -- not only the goodness you send in my direction, but also thank you for the goodness you contribute to the world. Thank you for, through your actions and your attitudes, choosing the right side.

description: On Scene shortly before 11:30am where the Waterbury Fire Department was called to the scene of a possible structure fire at 412 Watertown Ave. The first due companies found heavy smoke pushing out of a dry cleaning establishment and the liquor store in the adjacent store front. Since all occupants had evacuated the cleaners the crews were able to focus all of their attention on fighting the fire which was contained to the cleaners. Multiple hand lines were stretched, a supply line run from the hydrant approximately 250 feet up the street and a trench cut made in the roof by the truck company to bring it quickly under control. No injuries were sustained but the contents of the cleaners sustained smoke damage. The Fire Marshal's Office was called to the scene to investigate the fire and a representative Department of Health was called to inspect the liquor store and determine if the consumable commodities were not affected by the smoke from the fire.
